settings.title: Keep .atlas out of git
settings.summary: Add Atlas's per-project directory to each git project's .gitignore when it opens.
settings.doc: Keep Atlas's directory in each opened git project out of version control: `.atlas/` goes into the project's .gitignore (created if needed); a dev build's `.atlas-dev/` goes into .git/info/exclude. No-op on non-git projects.

settings.title: Atlas logs
settings.summary: Record sign-in, agent lifecycle, and file and browser opens into the Logs panel.
settings.doc: Record Atlas-internal events (sign-in, agent lifecycle, file and browser opens) into the Logs panel.

settings.title: Show hidden files
settings.summary: Show dotfiles and dot-directories in the explorer file tree.
settings.doc: Show dotfiles and dot-directories in the explorer file tree.

settings.title: Preferred editor
settings.summary: The external editor that Open in Editor uses for files and projects.
settings.doc: The external editor that "Open in <editor>" uses for a file or the project: an id such as "vscode", "cursor", "zed", "windsurf", "sublime", "xcode" or a JetBrains IDE ("idea", "webstorm", "pycharm"…), or "system" for the app your system opens the file with. Empty uses the first editor Atlas finds installed. An id that isn't installed falls back to that same choice. Files outside the project open in the system's app unless this names an editor.
settings.validation: an editor id; one that isn't installed falls back to the first one found

settings.title: Interface zoom
settings.summary: Scale the whole interface: text, icons and spacing together.
settings.doc: Interface zoom, where 1.0 is 100%. Also driven by Cmd +/-/0. Must be a number between 0.5 and 2.0.
settings.validation: finite, `0.5`–`2.0` inclusive

settings.title: Share usage data
settings.summary: Send privacy-preserving usage data to help improve Atlas. Never prompts, code, paths or keys.
settings.doc: Anonymous product telemetry. Opt-OUT: on by default, coarse metadata only, never file contents or prompts. See TELEMETRY.md.

settings.title: Link usage data to my account
settings.summary: While signed in, attribute usage data to your account instead of an anonymous device id.
settings.doc: Attribute telemetry to your signed-in Atlas account instead of the anonymous per-device id. Irrelevant while signed out, or while shareTelemetry is false — both gate it.

settings.title: Embedding model
settings.summary: The on-device model that embeds memory for search by meaning.
settings.doc: On-device embedding model, named by its directory. Normally managed for you by the Local Model Manager. Must not be empty.
settings.validation: non-empty

settings.title: Light theme
settings.summary: The theme Atlas uses while it's light: chrome, editor, terminal, diffs and syntax.
settings.doc: Theme id used while Atlas is light, for the whole app: chrome, editor, terminal, diffs and syntax. A theme with no light variant shows its dark one. Unknown ids fall back to "atlas" with a warning.
settings.validation: known theme id; an unknown id is logged and falls back to `"atlas"`

settings.title: Dark theme
settings.summary: The theme Atlas uses while it's dark: chrome, editor, terminal, diffs and syntax.
settings.doc: Theme id used while Atlas is dark, for the whole app. A theme with no dark variant shows its light one. Unknown ids fall back to "atlas" with a warning.
settings.validation: known theme id; an unknown id is logged and falls back to `"atlas"`

settings.title: Colour scheme
settings.summary: Follow the system, or always be light or dark.
settings.doc: Exactly "system", "dark" or "light": whether Atlas is light or dark, and so which of themeLight and themeDark it uses.
settings.validation: exactly one of these values; a missing requested variant falls back to the theme's other variant

settings.title: Theme overrides
settings.summary: A personal patch of base, palette and key colours applied on top of the active theme.
settings.doc: Optional user-local patch with base, palette and keys tables, applied after the active theme variant. Omitted when empty.
settings.validation: optional `base`, `palette`, and `keys` patch applied after the active theme variant; a bad entry is dropped, not fatal

settings.title: File icon theme
settings.summary: File and folder icons, chosen separately from the colour theme.
settings.doc: File and folder icons, on their own track from the color theme. "minimal" keeps Atlas's own lucide icons; anything else names a VS Code icon theme, bundled or installed from Open VSX.
settings.validation: a plain id (letters, digits, `.`, `-`, `_`) — it names a directory under `~/.config/atlas/icon-themes/`. `"minimal"` keeps Atlas's lucide icons. See `docs/reference/icon-themes.md`

settings.title: App icon
settings.summary: The icon in the Dock, Finder and Launchpad.
settings.doc: macOS app icon, by id: "dark" (the icon Atlas ships with) or "light". Any other than dark replaces the Dock and Finder icon. An id this Atlas does not know shows the default.
settings.validation: a plain id (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) from `src-tauri/icons/app-icons/app-icons.json` — today `"dark"` or `"light"`. An id this Atlas does not ship shows the default without rewriting the file

settings.title: Next-step suggestions
settings.summary: After each turn, the agent suggests two or three follow-ups as clickable chips.
settings.doc: Next-step suggestion chips in the session's per-turn card. Exactly "agent" or "off", nothing else.
settings.validation: exactly one of these two strings

settings.title: Switching agents in a session
settings.summary: What picking another agent does once a session has a conversation.
settings.doc: What picking another agent does to a session that has a conversation: "new-tab" keeps it and opens the new agent in a new tab, "handoff" switches in place and attaches it to the next message, "reset" switches in place and starts over.
settings.validation: exactly one of these three strings. An empty chat always switches in place and a running one always gets a new tab, whatever this says

settings.title: Save to memory before switching agents
settings.summary: Ask the agent you are leaving to save what it learned to shared memory first.
settings.doc: Before switching agents on a chat with a conversation, send the agent being left /remember (when it offers that command) and wait for it to save what it learned to shared memory. Costs one turn per switch.
settings.validation: — . Acts only on a chat with a conversation whose agent advertises `/remember` (the bundled `remember` skill); waits at most 3 minutes, and the user can switch at once

settings.title: Inline Git blame
settings.summary: Show who last changed the current line, and when, at the end of the line.
settings.doc: Inline git blame — a dim author/age/summary annotation trailing the active line in the editor.

settings.title: Auto-fetch from remote
settings.summary: Quietly fetch the open project so the Pull badge shows what the remote has. Never pulls.
settings.doc: Quietly `git fetch` the open project when it opens, when Atlas regains focus, and every few minutes, so the Pull badge shows what the remote has. Never pulls or touches your files.

settings.title: Keep awake while an agent is working
settings.summary: Prevent idle system sleep while an agent is running. The display can still turn off.
settings.doc: Keep the computer awake while an Atlas agent is actively running. Prevents idle system sleep; display can still turn off. No effect on Windows.
settings.validation: no effect on Windows

settings.title: Automatic updates
settings.summary: Check for a newer signed release on startup and prompt when one is available.
settings.doc: Check for a newer signed Atlas release on startup and prompt when one is available.

settings.title: Keep Atlas Agent's plugin catalog up to date
settings.summary: Download the latest curated plugin catalog when Atlas Agent starts.
settings.applies: the next time Atlas Agent starts
settings.doc: Let Atlas Agent download the latest curated plugin catalog when it starts — a network request at every launch. Applies the next time the agent starts.

settings.title: Mirror CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules into AGENTS.md
settings.summary: Keep a marked block of the project's AGENTS.md in step with CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules.
settings.doc: Mirror CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ into a marked block of the active project's AGENTS.md, kept current as they change, for any agent that reads AGENTS.md. Writes into the repository; text outside the block is never changed. Off: the block is taken back out.
settings.validation: — . See [Mirrored instructions](#mirrored-instructions-instructionsync)

settings.title: Skipped release
settings.summary: A release you chose to skip in the update prompt.
settings.doc: A release you chose to skip in the update prompt. Absent unless one was ignored — TOML has no null, so "unset" means the key simply isn't here. Delete the line to clear it; never write an empty string.

settings.title: Enter to send
settings.summary: Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Off: only ⌘/Ctrl+Enter sends.
settings.doc: Chat composer send gesture. true = Enter sends and Shift+Enter inserts a newline; false = only Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends either way.

settings.title: Let Atlas Agent navigate the app
settings.summary: Open files at a line, switch tabs and panels, and fill in a message or command for you.
settings.doc: Let Atlas Agent act on the window: open files at a line, switch tabs and panels, fill in a chat message, type a command for you to run. It never switches projects, sends for you or presses Enter. Off: its UI tools are withdrawn and every call is refused.

settings.title: Let Atlas Agent act in your organization
settings.summary: Read your organization's sessions, comments and conversations, and act there as you.
settings.doc: Let Atlas Agent act in your organization, as you: read the recorded sessions, comments, members and conversations of the organization a cloud-bound Project belongs to. Anything that reaches another person asks you first. Off: its organization tools are withdrawn and every call is refused.

settings.title: Let agents search code with Atlas
settings.summary: Give agents Atlas's in-process grep and find-files, which respect .gitignore and skip secrets.
settings.doc: Let agents search this project's code through Atlas: grep for text and find files by name, in-process, respecting .gitignore and never reading secret files such as .env. Off: the code tools are withdrawn and every call is refused; agents use their own shell instead.

settings.title: Nightly memory review
settings.summary: Once a day, propose changes to shared memory for you to review. Nothing applies without you.
settings.doc: Once a day, when there are new sessions, ask the memory model to propose changes to shared memory (add, merge, archive, rewrite, link). Proposals wait in Memory > Review; nothing is applied without you. Uses the same model and consent as extraction.

settings.title: Mirror memory as an Agent Memory Repo
settings.summary: Keep a read-only local git copy of each project's memory, outside the project.
settings.doc: Keep a read-only Agent Memory Repo mirror of each project's active memory, as a local git repository outside the project. No remote, nothing is pushed.

settings.title: Atlas is the only memory in Atlas sessions
settings.summary: Turn off each agent's own memory so every agent reads and writes the one shared memory.
settings.doc: Atlas's shared memory is the only memory in Atlas sessions: agents that keep their own memory, such as Claude Code's auto memory, start with it turned off. Off: each agent also keeps its own memory files.

settings.title: Notify on command success after
settings.summary: A terminal command that succeeds faster than this stays quiet. Failures always notify.
settings.doc: A successful command shorter than this many milliseconds never notifies. Must be between 0 and 3600000.

settings.title: Notifications
settings.summary: Every notification below. Sign-in problems always show.
settings.doc: Notifications master switch. Off silences every notification except sign-in problems, which always show.

settings.title: System notification
settings.summary: An OS banner for a permission request, a question, or a terminal asking for input.
settings.doc: OS banner for notifications that need you — a permission request, a question, a terminal asking for input. Shown only when you are away.

settings.title: Sound
settings.summary: A short sound with notifications that need you.
settings.doc: Sound for notifications that need you.

settings.title: System notification
settings.summary: An OS banner when an agent turn or terminal command finishes or fails.
settings.doc: OS banner when an agent turn or terminal command finishes or fails. Shown only when you are away.

settings.title: Sound
settings.summary: A short sound when something finishes or fails.
settings.doc: Sound for finished / failed notifications.

settings.title: System notification
settings.summary: An OS banner for context nearly full, rate limits, retries and stopped agents.
settings.doc: OS banner for warnings — context nearly full, rate limited, retrying, agent stopped.

settings.title: Sound
settings.summary: A short sound with warnings.
settings.doc: Sound for warnings.

settings.title: System notification
settings.summary: An OS banner for Chat direct messages and @mentions.
settings.doc: OS banner for Chat direct messages and @mentions. Shown only when you are away.

settings.title: Sound
settings.summary: A short sound with Chat notifications.
settings.doc: Sound for Chat notifications.

settings.title: Banner actions on permission requests
settings.summary: Show Allow once and Deny on a permission banner, so you can answer without opening Atlas.
settings.doc: Show Allow once / Deny buttons on permission banners. Off: the banner only opens the session.

settings.title: Notification kinds
settings.summary: One switch per kind of notification, from command finished to Git behind.
settings.doc: Notification kinds you switched off in Settings > Notifications, by id, e.g. ["terminal-done", "git-behind"]. Unknown ids are ignored; a kind that must always show (sign-in lost) cannot be silenced.
settings.validation: unknown ids are ignored

settings.title: Notify on agent finish after
settings.summary: An agent turn that finishes faster than this stays quiet. Failures and requests always notify.
settings.doc: An agent turn that finished faster than this many milliseconds stays quiet; failures and requests for you are never held back. 0 turns it off. Must be between 0 and 3600000.

settings.title: Favorite models
settings.summary: Models you starred in the composer's model picker.
settings.setIn: the star in the composer's model picker
settings.doc: Models you starred in the composer's model picker, as "agentType:modelId", e.g. ["claude-code:opus"]. Starred models open the picker on Favorites. Unknown entries are ignored.
settings.validation: entries are `agentType:modelId`; unknown entries are ignored

settings.title: Confirm before deleting a session
settings.summary: Ask first when you delete a session from the sidebar or history.
settings.doc: Ask before deleting a session from the sidebar or the history. A deleted session's transcript stays with its agent, but Atlas forgets the session. Settling never asks, because it can be undone.

settings.title: Confirm before quitting while an agent is running
settings.summary: Ask first when you quit Atlas with an agent in the middle of a turn.
settings.doc: Ask before quitting while an agent is in the middle of a turn, since quitting stops it. Quitting again while the question is open quits anyway.

settings.title: Continue sessions after a restart
settings.summary: A turn cut short when Atlas quits, crashes or updates carries on when Atlas opens again.
settings.doc: When Atlas quits, crashes or restarts to update while an agent is in the middle of a turn, the next launch opens that session and tells the agent to continue where it left off, with a row in the transcript saying so. Settled and snoozed sessions are left alone, and a turn that keeps getting cut short is let go after three tries in a row.

settings.title: Start with the last agent you picked
settings.summary: A new session starts on the agent you last chose in a composer, instead of the default agent.
settings.doc: A new session starts on the agent you last picked in a composer, by switching or with the agent shortcut, as long as it is still installed. Off, or before you have picked one, new sessions start on defaultAgent.

settings.title: Default agent
settings.summary: The agent a new session starts with.
settings.doc: The agent a new session starts with: "atlas-agent" for Atlas Agent, or the id of an installed ACP agent, such as "claude-code". An agent that isn't installed falls back to Atlas Agent.
settings.validation: a non-empty agent id; one that isn't installed falls back to Atlas Agent

settings.title: Session width
settings.summary: How wide the conversation and the composer may grow.
settings.doc: How wide the conversation and the composer may grow: "normal" (760 pixels), "wide" (1080 pixels) or "full" (the whole panel).
settings.validation: exactly one of these three strings

settings.title: Word wrap
settings.summary: Wrap long lines in files, diffs and a session's code blocks instead of scrolling sideways.
settings.doc: Wrap long lines in file tabs, diffs and a session's code blocks. Off: lines keep their shape and scroll sideways. The wrap button in a file's or the review diff's header flips this same setting.

settings.title: Sort sessions by
settings.summary: Order the sidebar's sessions by their latest activity or by when they started.
settings.doc: The order of sessions in the sidebar: "recent" puts the session with the latest activity first, "created" the one started most recently.
settings.validation: exactly one of these two strings

settings.title: Settle idle sessions after
settings.summary: A session with no activity for this many days moves to the sidebar's Settled shelf. 0 turns this off.
settings.doc: Days a session may sit idle before Atlas settles it: moves it to the Settled shelf at the bottom of the session sidebar, where it stays listed and resumable. A session that is running, waiting for you, pinned, snoozed, or that you un-settled since its last activity is left alone, and sending to a settled session brings it back. 0 turns auto-settling off; settling by hand still works. Must be between 0 and 90.

settings.title: Time format
settings.summary: Show times on a 12-hour or 24-hour clock, or as your system does.
settings.doc: The clock for every time of day Atlas shows: "12h", "24h", or "system" to follow your system's region settings.
settings.validation: exactly one of these three strings

settings.title: Interface font
settings.summary: The font for everything outside code and the terminal. Empty follows the theme, else the system font.
settings.doc: The font for Atlas's interface and chats, as a CSS font-family list such as "Inter, sans-serif". Empty uses the theme's font-sans if it sets one, else the system font. A font that isn't installed falls through to the next one in the list.
settings.validation: a CSS font-family list, at most 200 characters, with no `{`, `}`, `;`, `<` or `>`; empty uses the system font

settings.title: Code font
settings.summary: The font for the editor, diffs and code in chats. Empty follows the theme, else the default.
settings.doc: The font for the editor, diffs and code in chats, as a CSS font-family list such as "JetBrains Mono, monospace". Empty uses the theme's font-mono if it sets one, else the platform's monospace font. The terminal uses it too unless terminalFontFamily is set.
settings.validation: a CSS font-family list, at most 200 characters, with no `{`, `}`, `;`, `<` or `>`; empty uses the default

settings.title: Composer font
settings.summary: The font you type prompts in. Empty uses the interface font.
settings.doc: The font for the chat composer, as a CSS font-family list. Empty uses the interface font.
settings.validation: a CSS font-family list, at most 200 characters, with no `{`, `}`, `;`, `<` or `>`; empty uses the interface font

settings.title: Terminal font
settings.summary: The terminal's font. Empty uses the code font.
settings.doc: The terminal's font, as a CSS font-family list. Empty uses the code font. A font that isn't fixed-width misaligns columns.
settings.validation: a CSS font-family list, at most 200 characters, with no `{`, `}`, `;`, `<` or `>`; empty uses the code font

settings.title: Editor font size
settings.summary: The code editor's font size, in pixels.
settings.doc: The code editor's font size, in pixels. The interface zoom scales it along with everything else.

settings.title: Terminal font size
settings.summary: The terminal's font size, in pixels.
settings.doc: The terminal's font size, in pixels. The interface zoom scales it along with everything else.

settings.title: Hide whitespace changes
settings.summary: Leave out lines that only changed whitespace when you review a diff.
settings.doc: Leave out changes that are only whitespace in diffs you read: a file's diff, a commit, and a chat's changes. Diffs you stage from always show every change, since a patch without the whitespace no longer applies.

settings.title: Start files collapsed
settings.summary: Open a diff with each file collapsed to its header.
settings.doc: Open a diff, such as your changes or a commit, as a list of its files, each collapsed to its header; click a file to expand it. Off: every file starts expanded.

settings.title: Diff colours
settings.summary: Use the theme's green and red for changes, or blue and orange.
settings.doc: The colours for added and removed lines: "theme" uses the theme's green and red, "blue-orange" uses its blue and orange, which stay distinct with red-green colour blindness.
settings.validation: exactly one of these two strings

settings.title: Contrast
settings.summary: Strengthen or soften borders and secondary text across the interface.
settings.doc: Contrast of borders and secondary text, in percent of what the theme draws. Above 100 moves them toward the text colour, below 100 toward the background. Applies to every theme, the terminal and charts included.

settings.title: Turn rail
settings.summary: Show a tick for each turn down the left edge of a session. Hover one to preview it, click it to jump there.
settings.doc: The turn rail: a column of short ticks down the left edge of a session's transcript, one per turn. Hovering a tick previews the prompt and the start of the reply; clicking it jumps to that turn. Off hides the rail.

settings.title: New session background
settings.summary: A coloured glow behind a new session, or the plain background.
settings.doc: What sits behind a new, empty session: "glow" is a soft radial glow from the top edge in a colour from the palette (see welcomeGlowColor), "plain" is the theme's own background.
settings.validation: exactly one of these two strings

settings.title: Glow colour
settings.summary: A different colour each time, or always the same one.
settings.doc: The colour of the new-session glow. "random" picks a different one from the palette each time a new session opens; any other value always uses that colour. Each has a dark and a light version, matched to the colour scheme. Has no effect while welcomeBackground is "plain".
settings.validation: exactly one of these seven strings

settings.title: Settle sessions when their pull request merges
settings.summary: Move a session to Settled once its pull request merges or closes.
settings.doc: Settle a session once its linked pull request merges, when the merge came after you last worked in the session. A pull request that is closed without merging always settles its session. Settled sessions stay listed and resumable.

settings.title: Keep sessions with a pull request from settling
settings.summary: Idle auto-settling leaves a session with a linked pull request alone.
settings.doc: Auto-settling after days of inactivity (autoSettleAfterDays) leaves a session alone while it has a linked pull request. Merging or closing it can still settle the session (autoSettleOnMerge).

settings.title: Let agents act on watched pull requests
settings.summary: A watched pull request can prompt its session's agent when checks fail, reviews arrive or it conflicts.
settings.doc: When a session watches its pull request (the agent asked to, or you turned the watch on), a failing check, a new review or comment, or a conflict with the base sends the session's agent an update so it can act. Off: watches still track the pull request but never prompt an agent.

settings.title: Open pull request links in Atlas
settings.summary: Open a pull request of the project's repository in a tab instead of the browser.
settings.doc: Open a pull request link from a session, the sidebar or a transcript in Atlas's pull request tab when it belongs to the project's repository. Off, or a pull request of another repository: it opens in the browser.

settings.title: Default merge method
settings.summary: The method a pull request's Merge button starts on. Last used reuses your latest pick.
settings.doc: The method a pull request's Merge button starts on: "merge", "squash" or "rebase", or "last" for whichever you picked most recently on this device. A method the repository doesn't allow falls back to one it does.
settings.validation: exactly one of these four strings

settings.title: Remove agent credits when merging
settings.summary: Drop agent co-author and attribution lines from merge and squash messages, keeping human co-authors.
settings.doc: Remove recognized agent credit lines (an agent's Co-Authored-By trailer, a "Generated with" footer) from the message of a merge or squash Atlas performs, auto-merge included. Human co-authors are kept. Commits already on the branch are not rewritten.

settings.title: Review guides
settings.summary: A Guide tab on pull requests: an agent writes a tour of the change, stop by stop.
settings.doc: Show the Guide tab on pull requests, where an agent writes a tour of the change in reading order, with the calls a maintainer should make. The agent reads a checkout of the pull request's head and changes nothing.

settings.title: Guide agent
settings.summary: The agent that writes review guides. Empty uses the default agent for new sessions.
settings.doc: The agent that writes review guides: "atlas-agent" or an installed ACP agent's id, such as "claude-code". Empty uses defaultAgent. An agent that isn't installed falls back to Atlas Agent.
settings.validation: an agent id (letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`), at most 64 characters; empty uses the default agent

settings.title: Guide model
settings.summary: The model the guide's agent runs on. Empty keeps the agent's own default.
settings.doc: The model the guide's agent runs on, as that agent names it (the id after the colon in favoriteModels). The guide reads the change over many steps, so a stronger model helps. Empty keeps the agent's default; a model the agent doesn't offer is ignored.
settings.validation: one line, at most 200 characters; empty keeps the agent's default

settings.title: Guide instructions
settings.summary: Your preferences for review guides: what to show first, dwell on, or skip.
settings.doc: Your preferences for review guides, added to the guide's prompt: what to show first, dwell on or skip, and how long summaries should be. The guide's format and its coverage of every changed file stay the same.
settings.validation: at most 4000 bytes

settings.title: Scan new checkpoints for security issues
settings.summary: Check each new checkpoint's commit for leaked credentials, risky code and vulnerable dependencies, on this machine.
settings.doc: Scan each new checkpoint's commit in the background for leaked credentials, risky calls and dependencies with known advisories. Runs entirely on this machine; only the public advisory lists are downloaded. Results are stored with the checkpoint and not shown yet. Commits from before it was turned on are not scanned. Off in released builds and on in development builds unless this key is set.
